description:
🚀 HackSpher

HackSpher is a team of enthusiastic student innovators passionate about space exploration, technology, creativity, and problem-solving. We believe that innovative ideas can turn complex challenges into engaging and practical solutions.
summary: The Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, web-based 3D simulation designed to educate young students and future space explorers on planetary survival and habitat management. Built using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and Three.js within a lightweight single-file architecture, the simulator features realistic lunar and Martian environments, modular habitats with two-door airlock pressure cycling, and spacesuits with LED-lit helmets. Players navigate planetary surfaces, collect vital resource samples, maintain life support systems, and calibrate critical base machinery such as $O_2$ plants, solar arrays, and comms antennas. By integrating live NASA DONKI space weather telemetry and NASA Mars Rover photo APIs, the platform bridges real-world space science with immersive game-based learning, preparing trainees to handle space weather hazards like solar storms and dust devils.
details:
• What does it do or how does it work?
    The simulator provides a fully playable first-person 3D browser experience where trainees manage critical survival metrics ($O_2$, water, suit power, and radiation dose). Players navigate the terrain, pass through pressurized airlocks to enter the modular base, and interact with machinery (solar arrays, $O_2$ generators, and communication antennas) to complete mission objectives.
    • Languages & Frameworks: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Three.js (WebGL 3D engine).
    • APIs & Data Sources: NASA DONKI API (WSA-Enlil solar storm telemetry) and NASA Mars Rover Photos API.
    • Development Environment: VS Code with Live Server for instant browser deployment.
  • How is your project creative?
    It packs a complete 3D game engine, real-time physics, live NASA space weather telemetry, and an airlock simulation into a single, lightning-fast HTML file that deploys instantly without complex installs.
  • What factors did your team consider?
    Ease of accessibility for judges (zero-install browser execution), scientific accuracy (incorporating real solar storm data and radiation rates), and intuitive controls (supporting both keyboard WASD/E interactions and mobile touch joysticks).
